raw_text:
Client profile summary
- Age/sex: 45, female
- Medical: Type 2 diabetes on metformin; latest HbA1c 7.2% (above target)
- Goal: fat loss and improved glycaemic control
- Training environment: full gym available
- Assumptions (please confirm): medically cleared for moderate exercise, no contraindicating comorbidities (cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, proliferative retinopathy, severe neuropathy). No insulin or sulfonylureas (lower hypoglycaemia risk) — if medications change, modify guidance. Sleep and stress not specified; adjust if needed.

Overview and principles
- Primary aims: reduce body fat, improve insulin sensitivity, lower HbA1c toward target (<7% or individualized target), preserve/increase lean mass.
- Strategy: combine progressive resistance training (preserve/increase muscle — key for glucose disposal), aerobic and interval conditioning (improves VO2 max and insulin sensitivity), mobility and recovery, and structured nutrition focusing on moderate energy deficit, distributed protein, controlled carbohydrate timing/quality, and attention to blood glucose responses.
- Safety notes for diabetes: monitor for hypoglycaemia symptoms (less likely on metformin alone but possible if other meds added), encourage carrying fast-acting carbs if needed, hydrate, avoid sudden heavy exertion if known cardiovascular risk.
- Targets: moderate energy deficit ~300–500 kcal/day for steady fat loss (~0.5–1.0 lb/week); protein 1.2–1.6 g/kg BW/day to spare muscle (use upper end during deficit), resistance training 3×/week plus 2 cardio/conditioning sessions, progressive overload.

If client weight is unknown, use percentages — I will offer relative prescriptions. Please provide weight if you want calorie and absolute protein numbers.

Nutrition plan (diabetes-specific)
- Energy: aim for a daily deficit of ~300–500 kcal from maintenance. If you give current weight, I can estimate maintenance; otherwise use a general guideline: reduce typical intake by ~15–20%.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight/day. Distribute evenly across meals (e.g., 25–40 g protein per meal) to support muscle protein synthesis and glycaemic control.
- Carbohydrates: moderate, quality-first approach. Target ~30–40% of calories from carbs initially (adjust based on glucose responses). Prioritise low-GI and high-fiber carbs: non-starchy vegetables, legumes, oats, quinoa, berries, apples, sweet potato. Avoid refined sugars and high-GI snacks.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories, emphasise unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, avocados, fatty fish).
- Meal timing and distribution: 3 regular meals plus 1–2 small snacks if needed. Pair carbs with protein and a little fat to blunt postprandial glucose spikes (e.g., oats + whey + nuts; chicken salad with avocado + lentils).
- Pre/post-exercise nutrition: for morning workouts in a fasted state, monitor glucose and consider a small carbohydrate-containing snack (15–20 g carb) if client experiences dizziness; otherwise resistance sessions are fine fasted. For longer cardio >45–60 min, have 20–30 g carb available. Post-workout: 20–30 g protein + 20–30 g carbs to support recovery and refill glycogen.
- Fiber: ≥25–30 g/day to help glycaemic control.
- Sodium, alcohol: limit alcohol (moderate) and be cautious about late-night carb-heavy snacks. Limit highly processed foods.
- Hydration and timing of metformin: continue per physician; metformin generally safe with exercise.
- Monitor blood glucose: encourage client to check fasting glucose and optionally pre/post-exercise readings for a few sessions to learn individual responses. Keep a log of meals + glucose + symptoms for 2 weeks to refine carb distribution.
- Supplements (optional): vitamin D if deficient; consider omega-3 if low fish intake. Whey or other protein supplement to hit protein targets. Cinnamon has limited evidence; follow medical advice.

Programme structure (12 weeks) — phases
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Adaptation + foundation — build movement quality, baseline conditioning, and teach nutrition habits. Resistance 3×/week.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength + increased intensity — progressive overload, introduce metabolic conditioning and HIIT once/week.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Fat-loss consolidation + peak conditioning — higher density sessions, maintained strength, targeted cardio to maximize energy expenditure while protecting muscle.

Weekly schedule template (example)
- 3x resistance training (full-body, 45–60 min): Mon / Wed / Fri
- 2x cardio/conditioning (30–40 min): Tue / Sat (one steady-state, one interval)
- 1–2x mobility / active recovery (short sessions): Thu / Sun
- 1 rest day if needed: rotate as client prefers

Progression principles
- Increase weight when client can complete upper range of reps with good form for 2 consecutive sessions (≈2.5–5% load increase).
- Track RPE (aim 7–8/10 on last sets in strength phase).
- Maintain protein and calorie targets even as weight drops.
- Reassess weight and fasting glucose every 2 weeks; adjust calories if weight loss stalls.

Detailed week-by-week plan

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Adaptation, technique, baseline conditioning
Goals: learn exercise technique, build consistency, start moderate deficit, distribute protein, increase NEAT.

Rules: warm-up 8–10 min before sessions (5 min bike/row + dynamic mobility), cool-down and stretching 5–8 min after.

Weeks 1–2 (Foundation)
Resistance sessions (Mon / Wed / Fri) — full body, 3 sets each unless noted. Rests 60–90s.
- Squat variation (Goblet squat or barbell box squat): 3 × 8–10
- Push (Dumbbell bench press or machine press): 3 × 8–10
- Pull (Seated cable row or one-arm DB row): 3 × 8–10
- Romanian deadlift (or hip hinge with kettlebell): 3 × 8–10
- Overhead press (DB or machine): 2–3 × 8–10
- Single-leg exercise (split squat or step-up): 2 × 8 per leg
- Core: Pallof press or dead bug: 2 × 10–15 each side

Conditioning (Tue): steady-state cardio — 30–40 min moderate intensity (brisk treadmill walk, incline walk, stationary bike) aiming for conversational pace.
Conditioning (Sat): low-impact intervals — 20–25 min total (e.g., 1:1 work-rest 30s hard/30s easy on bike or elliptical) or incline walk intervals: 1 min faster / 1 min slow × 10.

Mobility/active recovery (Thu or Sun): 15–20 min mobility (thoracic rotation, hamstring and hip mobility, ankle mobility), foam rolling.

Weeks 3–4 (Progress foundation)
Same 3x resistance but increase intensity:
- Move to 3–4 sets on main lifts; rep ranges 6–10 for compound lifts. Example:
- Back squat or leg press: 3–4 × 6–8
- Bench press or incline DB press: 3 × 6–8
- Bent-over row or chest-supported row: 3 × 6–8
- Deadlift variation (RDL or trap bar): 3 × 6–8
- DB overhead press: 3 × 8
- Walking lunges: 2 × 10–12 steps
- Core: plank variations 3 × 30–60 s

Conditioning: increase one session to 35–45 min steady-state; interval session increase to 25–30 min with 45s work/45s rest.

Nutrition focus for Phase 1:
- Calculate estimated calorie goal (e.g., 300–500 kcal deficit). If unknown, start with a modest 15% reduction.
- Aim for protein 1.2–1.4 g/kg/day; distribute across 3 meals.
- Start food/activity/glucose log for 2 weeks.
- Replace high-GI snacks with vegetables/protein snacks; practice pairing carbs with protein.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Strength and metabolic conditioning
Goals: increase strength (heavier loads, lower reps on key lifts), increase overall energy expenditure with metabolic circuits and HIIT once weekly.

Weekly template similar; resistance still Mon/Wed/Fri, cardio Tue/Sat.

Weeks 5–6
Resistance (Mon)
- Squat (Back squat or front squat): 4 × 5–6
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 6–8
- Bench press or incline: 4 × 5–6
- Bent-over row: 3 × 6–8
- Accessory superset (e.g., DB lateral raise + triceps pushdown): 2 × 12 each
- Core: hanging knee raises 3 × 10–12

Resistance (Wed) — Posterior emphasis
- Deadlift or trap bar deadlift: 4 × 4–6
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 × 8 per leg
- Pull-up or lat pulldown: 3 × 6–8
- Single-arm DB press: 3 × 8–10
- Hamstring curl: 2 × 10–12
- Core: anti-rotation holds 3 × 10–15s

Resistance (Fri) — Mixed metabolic day
- Circuit (3 rounds): 8–10 reps each, minimal rest between exercises, 90s between rounds:
  - Leg press or goblet squat
  - Incline DB press
  - Seated cable row
  - Kettlebell swings (light–moderate)
  - Farmer carry 40–60 m
- Finish with 2 rounds of high-rep glute bridges 12–15

Conditioning
- Tue: interval session (HIIT) — 20–25 min: 30s high intensity / 60s easy × 12–15. Use bike or rower to reduce joint stress.
- Sat: 40–45 min steady-state moderate intensity (elliptical, incline walk).

Nutrition adjustments in Phase 2:
- Increase protein toward 1.4–1.6 g/kg/day to support strength demands.
- Continue moderate carb control; consider timing 30–60 g carbs pre-workout if energy low, and 20–30 g carbs post-workout with 20–30 g protein.
- Emphasise low-GI evening meals to reduce nocturnal glucose excursions.
- Encourage 25–30 g fiber daily.
- If weight loss slower than desired after 2–3 weeks, reduce daily calories by another 100–150 kcal or increase NEAT/cardio; do not exceed aggressive deficits.

Weeks 7–8
Progression: increase load on main lifts. Add a metabolic conditioning session into a resistance day occasionally.
- Resistance: main lifts 3–5 sets, reps 4–6 for strength exercises and 8–12 for accessory work.
- Introduce EMOM (every minute on the minute) sets for conditioning: e.g., 12 min EMOM alternating 8 kettlebell swings and 6 burpees (modify burpees to step-back burpees if needed).
- Cardio: one HIIT session (20–25 min) and one longer steady 45–50 min low-to-moderate intensity.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Fat-loss consolidation and maintenance of strength
Goals: maximize fat loss through training density and interval volume while protecting lean mass.

Weeks 9–10
Resistance (Mon/Wed/Fri) — keep 3 strength sessions but slightly increase density:
- Two heavy compound sessions (Mon, Wed) and one higher-rep hypertrophy/metcon session (Fri).
Mon (strength)
- Back squat: 4 × 4–6
- Bench press: 4 × 4–6
- Barbell row: 3 × 6–8
- Accessory: Glute-ham raise or Nordic curl 3 × 8–10

Wed (strength/pulling emphasis)
- Deadlift: 4 × 3–5 (substitute trap bar if lower back concern)
- Overhead press: 4 × 6
- Pull-ups/assisted: 3 × 6–8
- Single-leg RDL: 2 × 8–10 per leg

Fri (metabolic/hypertrophy circuit)
- Circuit: 4 rounds, minimal rest:
  - Leg press 10
  - Incline DB press 10
  - Cable row 10
  - Kettlebell swing 15
  - Plank 45 s

Conditioning
- Tue: HIIT 20–25 min (e.g., 40s hard/20s easy)
- Sat: longer brisk walk/hike or bike 50–60 min moderate; focus on adherence and NEAT.

Weeks 11–12
Polish and taper slightly in week 12 for recovery and reassessment.
- Maintain loads on strength lifts but reduce volume in week 12 (cut sets by 20–30%).
- Keep one HIIT and one steady session weekly.
- Emphasise technique and mindfully increase rest between heavy sets if RPE very high.

Sample session progression notes
- Example progression for squat: Week 1 goblet 3×10; Week 3 barbell 3×8; Week 5 barbell 4×5 heavier; Week 9 barbell 4×4 heavier.
- Use RPE 7–8 on most top sets in strength phase. In final phase, prioritize quality and recovery.

Recovery, sleep, and stress
- Aim for 7–8 hours sleep nightly. Poor sleep increases insulin resistance and appetite.
- Active recovery days: walking, mobility, foam rolling.
- Deload/taper week 12: reduce volume to consolidate strength and allow metabolic adaptation.
- Manage stress with mindfulness, breathing or low-impact activities; chronic stress raises blood glucose.

Monitoring and progression
- Recheck HbA1c after ~12 weeks to see clinical improvement (HbA1c reflects ~3 months of control).
- Weekly/biweekly measures: body weight, waist circumference, fasting glucose (morning), training logs.
- Adjust calories if weight loss stalls for >2–3 weeks (reduce 100–200 kcal or increase activity). Avoid too aggressive deficits which can raise cortisol and harm glycaemia.
- If client experiences recurrent hypoglycaemia, or any chest pain, dizziness, unusual symptoms — stop exercise and seek medical review.

Practical meal examples (diabetes-friendly)
- Breakfast: Greek yogurt (or plant-based high-protein) + 30 g oats + 20 g whey + berries + 1 tbsp nut butter.
- Lunch: Large mixed salad with grilled chicken, 1/2 cup quinoa, plenty of non-starchy veg, olive oil dressing.
- Snack: Apple + 20–30 g almonds or 1 string cheese.
- Dinner: Baked salmon, roasted broccoli, 1/2 sweet potato, mixed greens.
- Post-workout snack (if needed): whey shake (20–25 g protein) + banana or small rice cake (15–25 g carbs).

Other considerations specific to diabetes
- Encourage regular medical review and potential collaboration with prescribing clinician/dietitian. Metformin is weight-neutral/causes mild appetite suppression; weight loss and increased activity may affect glycaemic control — communicate any medication changes.
- Foot care: ensure proper footwear and inspect feet given diabetes.
- If peripheral neuropathy or retinopathy present, modify high-impact activities accordingly.
- Consider referral to a registered dietitian for personalized meal planning and carbohydrate counting if client interested.

12-week metrics to track
- Body weight and waist circumference (weekly for weight, every 2 weeks for waist)
- Training load progression (weights, reps)
- Fasting glucose (daily or several times/week initially)
- Energy levels, sleep, subjective appetite
- HbA1c baseline and at 12 weeks (or per physician schedule)

If you want:
- I can calculate individualized calorie and macronutrient targets if you provide current bodyweight, height, activity level.
- I can produce printable session cards or demonstrations/progressions for each exercise.
- I can adapt the plan for comorbidities (e.g., joint issues, neuropathy) or different availability (home-only).
